frameworks.name: Proof-Promise-Plan Intro Framework
frameworks.definition: A three-part opening structure for webinars and sales presentations: Proof (a result for someone like the prospect), Promise (exactly what they will get), Plan (expectations for the session duration and flow). Used at both webinar and sales call opening.

frameworks.name: Value Equation
frameworks.definition: Four-lever framework for maximizing perceived offer value: maximize Dream Outcome, decrease Risk (use proof), decrease Time (show speed), decrease Hard (show ease).

frameworks.name: Three-Pillar Pitch
frameworks.definition: A pitch structure that condenses a multi-step process into three named buckets; complexity of the presentation scales inversely with buyer implementation burden — simpler for DIY/DWY, more steps for DFY.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi reports that a webinar-based portfolio company plateaued at ~$570,000/month for six months. After implementing multi-channel show-up reminders (9-email sequence, SMS, behavior-triggered content, and voicemail drops) and webinar structure changes, the company grew from $569,000 to $860,000/month in monthly revenue, surpassing a $10M annual run rate, with a 30.7% profit margin.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: webinar-based sales model
founder doing one webinar per week
claims.mechanism: Increasing show rate and booking rate from the same ad spend produced compounding improvements across the acquisition pipeline without changing ad budget.

numbers.axis: monthly revenue before vs. after optimization

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that improving webinar show-up rate from 18% to 24% (a 33% relative increase) produces the same revenue impact as a 33% increase in close rate, but is easier to achieve because it can be automated as one-time work rather than requiring ongoing sales coaching.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: webinar-based acquisition funnel
claims.mechanism: Show-up rate improvement multiplies the pool entering the sales call without requiring any change in sales skills or scripts; automation makes the gain permanent.

numbers.axis: relative improvement in revenue-generating pipeline events

anchors.region: equivalent close rate improvement needed to match

bounded_by: Does not apply if the show-up rate improvement is already saturated or the webinar itself is low quality

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that SMS reminders have a 95–99% open rate and, among all multi-channel webinar reminder tactics (email sequence, SMS, behavior-triggered content, voicemail), SMS is likely the single largest driver of show-up rate improvement.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: audiences who are less email-responsive (e.g., blue-collar industries)
claims.mechanism: SMS delivers the message to virtually all recipients regardless of inbox habits, unlike email which can be missed or filtered.

anchors.value: lower, variable; often filtered to promo tabs

bounded_by: Do not abuse SMS; a few strategically placed texts is the advised approach

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that the three most important webinar reminder touchpoints are 24 hours before, the morning of, and one hour prior, and these three slots are the mandatory SMS sends in any reminder sequence.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: live or automated webinar registration sequences

claims.text: Alex Hormozi reports that re-scripting the first five minutes of a three-hour sales presentation for a different Acquisition.com portfolio company produced a 20% increase in close rates, demonstrating that opening framing has disproportionate impact relative to its share of total presentation time.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: long-form sales presentation (approximately 3 hours)
Acquisition.com portfolio company
claims.mechanism: The first five minutes establishes the frame and audience retention; losing audience attention early forfeits the rest of the pitch entirely.

numbers.axis: close rate change from intro rewrite

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that on webinar sales calls, the opening framing should immediately state the call's purpose as qualification for a guarantee or bonus, not a sales pitch, which shifts the buyer into a position of seeking approval rather than resisting a sell. He frames this as a takeaway framing technique.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: sales calls following a webinar
offer has a guarantee or scarce bonus that can be withheld on qualification grounds
claims.mechanism: Telling prospects they must qualify for something (a guarantee, bonus, or start date) inverts the power dynamic: they lean in to earn the offer rather than resist a pitch, which reduces objections and increases conversion.
bounded_by: Requires a genuine qualification criterion or guarantee that can be credibly withheld

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that sales process congruence — matching messaging from ad through webinar headline, webinar body, sales call opening, and onboarding — produces significantly more revenue than misaligned multi-step funnels, even though each individual step seems obvious.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: multi-step acquisition funnels: ad → webinar → sales call → onboarding
claims.mechanism: Each step reinforces the same value promise, so the prospect never experiences cognitive dissonance or feels misled, which lubricates each successive conversion event.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that during sales call discovery, salespeople should stay chunked up at the highest level possible and avoid detailed technical questions, because detailed questions transfer control of the conversation to the prospect and risk triggering objections the salesperson then has to answer.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: B2B or high-ticket service sales calls following a webinar or VSL
claims.mechanism: When the salesperson answers the prospect's detailed questions, the salesperson becomes the responder and loses conversational direction; staying high-level keeps the salesperson as the questioner and the prospect as the answerer, maintaining sales momentum.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that for done-for-you (DFY) offers, presenting a large number of steps (e.g., 11, 27, 38) in the pitch increases close rates because it signals complexity the buyer does not want to do themselves; for do-it-yourself (DIY) and done-with-you (DWY) offers, a simple 3-part pitch increases close rates because the buyer must believe they can execute it.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: DFY offers: present 11–38 steps to emphasize implementation complexity
DIY/DWY offers: present 3 pillars to emphasize achievability
claims.mechanism: For DFY, showing complexity creates relief ('I don't want to do this — you do it for me'); for DIY/DWY, simplicity creates confidence ('I can follow this system with help').
bounded_by: DWY is treated as DIY-plus-accountability; same simplicity principle applies

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that a webinar show-up rate below 25% indicates a problem worth fixing, and that 25% or higher is a reasonable target for a webinar with a multi-day lead time between opt-in and broadcast.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: webinar-based acquisition funnels
lead time between opt-in and webinar of several days

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that a post-webinar sales call close rate of 14% is bad and signals a broken sales process; after fixing framing, discovery, pitch simplification, and execution discipline, the close rate for the portfolio company rose to 35% — a 2.4x improvement.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: sales calls following a live webinar
B2B or high-ticket offer

numbers.axis: sales call close rate before vs. after optimization

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that incentivizing salespeople on cash collected (rather than contracts signed or payment plans initiated) aligns closer incentives with business cash flow and produces harder, higher-quality closes; with a 5x difference in commission per deal between payment plan and paid-in-full, closers have a strong financial reason to pursue paid-in-full conversions.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: businesses offering both paid-in-full and installment payment plans on the same product
claims.mechanism: Commission tied to cash collected aligns the closer's financial incentive with the business's cash flow and LTV quality; a closer paid 10% commission earns $200 on a $2k installment first payment vs. $1,000 on a $10k paid-in-full — a 5x difference — which motivates more assertive closes and self-selects for motivated buyers.

numbers.axis: closer commission per sale by payment structure (10% commission on $10k product)

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that routing the best leads to the best closers and worst leads to worst closers is a universally applicable sales optimization: it maximizes total closed revenue at the top and minimizes opportunity cost at the bottom.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: sales teams with meaningful variance in individual closer performance
claims.mechanism: High performers convert higher-intent prospects at higher rates; pairing them compounds both advantages. Weak closers on weak leads minimizes revenue lost to poor execution.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that when a founder hands off a function and performance statistics decline, this is abdication (not delegation); true delegation produces equal or better performance because a skilled person with more focused time should outperform a divided founder.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: founder handing off sales or revenue-generating functions to less-experienced hires
claims.mechanism: If the replacement has equivalent skill and more dedicated time, output should improve; declining stats after handoff signal undertrained replacement or incomplete documentation, not an inherent limit of delegation.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that tracking granular sub-KPIs (show rate, offer rate, close rate, specific objection categories) rather than only close rate allows personalized coaching per salesperson and surfaces where individual closers break down, producing faster improvement than top-level reporting alone.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: sales teams of 2+ closers with measurable pipeline stages
claims.mechanism: Top-level close rate aggregates multiple sources of failure; sub-KPI tracking isolates whether a closer fails at showing up, making the offer, or handling specific objections, enabling targeted rather than generic coaching.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that measurement itself functions as an intervention: having sales reps report daily on show rate, schedule rate, and close rate changes their behavior and improves those metrics independent of any coaching or script change, because the reported pain forces action.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: cadence short enough that reps can change behavior between reporting periods (daily or weekly)
claims.mechanism: Visibility into a negative metric creates emotional discomfort; the discomfort motivates behavior change without external instruction. The pain of seeing a bad number is itself the coaching signal.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that for businesses already generating revenue, improving existing channels (more volume or better execution on current tactics) is a better risk-adjusted move than launching new channels, because current channels are already proven to work in principle.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: businesses with at least one functioning acquisition channel that has not been pushed to saturation
claims.mechanism: An improvement to an existing proven system compounds within the same unit economics; a new channel introduces unknown variables and requires a full validation cycle before delivering reliable returns.
bounded_by: Does not apply when the existing channel is genuinely saturated or structurally broken

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that a business that does not communicate its real constraints (limited slots, live timing, scarcity) gets zero benefit from those constraints, because perceived scarcity and urgency — not actual scarcity — drive buyer action.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: webinar or sales funnel with real but uncommunicated capacity constraints
claims.mechanism: Buyers respond to perceived conditions; if a deadline or scarcity is real but unannounced, it has no behavioral effect. Stating true facts (we have N slots, this is live) is both ethical and commercially necessary.
bounded_by: Scarcity must be real or framed with hedging language ("typically", "often") to remain compliant

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that in a business with thin profit margins, a 50% increase in top-line revenue can produce a 5x increase in profit because incremental revenue above the fixed-cost threshold drops through to net at a much higher rate than average margin.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: businesses with meaningful fixed cost bases and low current net margins (e.g., 10%)
claims.mechanism: Fixed costs are already covered by baseline revenue; each incremental dollar of revenue above that threshold contributes fully to profit net of variable costs, producing a disproportionate profit multiplier.

numbers.axis: profit multiplier from revenue increase at 10% net margin

bounded_by: Assumes fixed costs do not scale proportionally with the revenue increase

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that using the word 'sold out' for time slots during a live webinar close — as each slot is booked — is a compliant and effective scarcity tactic because it states factual information while framing the booking activity as purchasing behavior, which primes remaining attendees to buy.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: live webinars with real booking slots
host can see booking activity in real time
claims.mechanism: The phrase 'sold out' primes a buying frame; calling out specific booked slots in real time creates visible social proof and urgency simultaneously, accelerating booking frenzy among remaining attendees.
bounded_by: Must reflect actual slot status to remain truthful; cannot fabricate sold-out status

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that getting a prospect to explicitly invite the pitch — by asking 'where do you want to go from here?' after summarizing their fit — increases pitch receptivity because the prospect has given permission to be sold, eliminating the defensive posture that unsolicited pitching triggers.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: discovery-to-pitch transition in high-ticket sales calls
claims.mechanism: Permission granted by the prospect reframes the pitch as a response to their request rather than a push; this removes the adversarial dynamic and positions the salesperson as fulfilling the prospect's stated desire.

examples.text: Alex Hormozi's Acquisition.com portfolio company was running one webinar per week, meaning opt-ins sometimes waited nearly a week before the event. Show rates were 18%. After adding a 9-email sequence (hitting pain, speed, ease, and being stuck), SMS reminders, behavior-triggered behind-the-scenes content for engaged openers, and voicemail drops — covering all four consumption preferences — show rates rose from 18% to 24%, a 33% relative improvement from the same opt-in volume.

During the webinar, to create booking urgency, the host asked attendees to type in the chat when they booked a call slot. The host then called out names in real time ('I see Rosie booked, I see John booked') and announced when specific days and time blocks were 'sold out' — even when total remaining slots were few — by chunking availability into morning and afternoon blocks. This created a visible booking frenzy that increased the booking rate from the webinar by 33%, lifting total booked calls from 58 to 102 per webinar event (a 77% increase).

The Acquisition.com team identified that their portfolio company's webinar was losing most of its audience in the first few minutes. They scripted a faster intro using the Proof-Promise-Plan framework — immediately identifying a relatable result, stating exactly what attendees would get, and setting session expectations — rather than the prior slow rapport-building opening. Combined with three other webinar changes (stating the webinar was live, announcing qualification criteria, and adding scarcity through slot call-outs), the booking rate from the webinar increased 33%.

Before optimization, the portfolio company's sales call opening was: 'Hey, how's it going? My name's so-and-so. How's your week going? Cool, great — I know we have limited time here, so are you ready to jump in? Do you have pen and paper?' After the rewrite, the opener became: 'Hey, my name's John. I have a background in [specific relevant domain]. I work closely with [the webinar host they saw]. I'd love to know what resonated most with you.' Then: 'The real purpose of this call is to see if you qualify for our guarantee. Not everyone does, and it's based on these three factors.' This shift from rapport-building to immediate takeaway framing contributed to the close rate rising from 14% to 35%.

The Acquisition.com team discovered the portfolio company's sales discovery was going too deep into tactical details, losing conversational control to prospects asking detailed questions. They also found closers were not roleplaying or practicing discovery. After introducing regular role-play sessions, tracking granular sub-KPIs (show rate per closer, offer rate, close rate, objection categories), cutting the calendar in half for below-KPI reps (with one-to-two weeks to recover or exit), and routing the best leads to the best closers, close rate moved from 14% to 35%.

practices.text: Send exactly three SMS reminders before any webinar or live event: the night before (24 hours prior), the morning of, and one hour prior. These are the non-negotiable slots in any reminder sequence.

When a live webinar is running, state explicitly that it is live — mention the time, weather, or current events — to signal real-time presence. The live frame improves engagement and conversion even when the mechanism is unclear.

In your webinar or sales presentation, analyze attendance drop-off data to find where the audience leaves, then prioritize fixing those sections. Spikes in engagement indicate content worth expanding; steep drop-offs indicate content to rebuild.

Do not give equally weighted calls to all closers. Allocate the best-quality inbound leads to the highest-performing closers; manage out persistent underperformers by cutting their calendar allocation before terminating.

If you do something live that creates an advantage (scarcity of slots, a real deadline, a live event), explicitly communicate it. You receive zero benefit from real constraints you do not communicate.
Before obsessing over new tactics or channels, watch recordings of your own sales calls and webinars to find where prospects disengage or object. Fix the identified breakdowns before adding volume.

Structure webinar qualification criteria and call booking scarcity so that both are true statements (actual team size, actual slot count). Hedge frequency claims with 'typically' or 'often' rather than absolute guarantees when necessary.
